entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Latinius Pacatus Drepanius, one of the Latin panegyrists, flourished at the end of the 4th century AD.

Born of unknown parentage, Drepanius rose to prominence as a poet and orator in late antiquity.

His works, while largely lost to time, demonstrate the enduring influence of classical Roman culture on the artistic and literary traditions of the Western world.

Drepanius's legacy can be seen in the many imitations of his style that followed him, from the writings of St. Augustine to the development of the sonnet in Italy.

In the annals of history, Latinius Pacatus Drepanius stands as a testament to the power of cultural continuity and the indelible mark left by the classical world on the modern era.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Latinius Pacatus Drepanius played a significant role in shaping the literary canon of the Western world, influencing the development of Christian hymnody and the sonnet form, and contributing to the cultural exchange network that emerged during the late 4th century AD.
